item.title: Run Arbitrary Command on Yarn
item.description:
Generic Steps to Submit an App to YARN #

  1. Prepare application resources. Package the client and ApplicationMaster code, then make sure YARN can localize them.

    java 
    FileSystem fs = FileSystem.get(conf);
Path stagingDir = new Path(fs.getHomeDirectory(), ".yarn-binary-demo/" + appId);
fs.mkdirs(stagingDir);

Map<String, LocalResource> amLocalResources = new HashMap<>();
Path appJarDst = new Path(stagingDir, YarnBinaryDemoSupport.APP_JAR_NAME);
amLocalResources.put(
 YarnBinaryDemoSupport.APP_JAR_NAME,
 YarnBinaryDemoSupport.copyToHdfsAsLocalResource(fs, new Path(appJar), appJarDst));

  2. Create a YARN client and allocate a new application ID. The client connects to the ResourceManager and asks for a fresh application handle.

item.title: Hadoop Overview
item.description:
Apache Hadoop is a Java framework for storing data across a cluster and executing distributed applications near that data. Its original batch model combines three separate responsibilities:

  1. HDFS stores one logical filesystem across machines.
  2. YARN allocates cluster resources and launches application processes.
  3. MapReduce divides a batch computation into map, shuffle, and reduce phases.

Hadoop Common supplies the configuration, filesystem abstractions, security support, native-library integration, and command launchers used by those projects. Separating the responsibilities matters because HDFS can store data for applications other than MapReduce, and YARN can schedule application frameworks other than MapReduce.
